To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the E.coli dihydroxyacetones (Dha)kinase complex reveals that Dhaprotein DhaL binds to the active site of DhaK in a manner that allows Dhaprotein Dhaprotein Dhal to phosphorylate the permanently bound substrate Dha, and that His56K, Asp109K, and His218K are involved in the catalysis of covalent substrate Dha binding and subsequent phosphorylation.

the structure of the Dha kinase complex reveals that DHA is covalently linked to the enzyme via the 1-position of DHA, and that the structure of DHA in the complex is different from that of DHA bound noncovalently to DHA.

the crystal structure of DhaK– DhaL, combined with mutagenesis and biochemical studies, reveals the catalytic mechanism of DhaK, a covalently bound kinase, and that this mechanism differs from that of other kinases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, and mechanism of dihydroxy-acetone (Dha)-kinase, an enzyme that is essential for the metabolism of Dha, a precursor of the polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs).
understanding of the structure and function of dihydroxyactone kinase, which is a member of the family of kinases that are involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates.
the structural basis of the unusual catalytic mechanism of the E. coli dihydroxyacetones kinase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the covalently bound substrate in DhaK is not only a structural feature, but also a key element in substrate positioning and catalysis.

the Dha kinase is an enzyme with a novel mechanism for binding and phosphorylation of the substrate, which is covalently attached to one subunit, and that this is accomplished by a highly conserved active-site residue, His218K.

Dha kinase is a novel enzyme that uses the phosphoenyl pyruvate PTS as the source of a high energy phosphoryl group, and that the active site is composed of two subunits, DhaK and DhaL, which form a complex that is stabilized by the covalently bound ADP co-substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the covalently bound substrate in dihydroxyacetoned kinases is oriented in a way that is optimal for phosphoryl transfer, and that the active site residues of Dha kinase are highly conserved and play a role in catalysis.
the structure of the complex shows how DhaK and DhaL interact and how DhaK undergo conformational changes when DhaL binds.
the Dha kinase complex is a unique enzyme that is able to catalyze the covalent binding of Dha and the subsequent phosphorylation and release of Dha-phosphate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
covalent attachment of substrate to the active site of the enzyme is an important feature of this kinase and is essential for catalysis.
the Dha kinase complex is a unique example of a two-subunit enzyme with a covalently bound substrate.
Dha kinases are a unique example of a kinase that binds the substrate covalently to the active site and that they use the same catalytic mechanism as other kinases.
